anf_compare.notes: Translated from the PG 77 Greek. No published English version was used for wording.

bible_refs.method: wording: 'εὐλαβεῖς ποιεῖτε τοὺς υἱοὺς Ἰσραήλ'; LXX Leviticus 15:31 'καὶ εὐλαβεῖς ποιήσετε τοὺς υἱοὺς Ισραηλ ἀπὸ τῶν ἀκαθαρσιῶν αὐτῶν'
bible_refs.note: Same verse number in the LXX and the Hebrew. The Hebrew reads 'keep the people of Israel separate from their uncleanness', so the English follows Cyril's Greek (εὐλαβής, careful).

choices.english: whose way of life deserves admiration
choices.why: A litotes ('a not unadmirable way of life'); the positive English keeps the praise without a double negative.

choices.english: and that also contributes to the good name
choices.why: τελέω εἰς: to tend toward, contribute to; ὑπόληψις here is the churches' standing in others' eyes.
They are made to stumble by what they see; plain modern English.
To seize and carry along: the men hurry the bishops into ordaining them.

pass_a_gloss: Of the same [author] to the bishops in Libya and Pentapolis. [Preface (prooimion).] Of everything useful (chrēsimos) and necessary (anankaios) for the building up (oikodomē) of the peoples (laos), and accomplishing also toward the esteem (hypolēpsis) of the holy churches, it is needful (chrē) to take care (phrontis). For it has been written (graphō) that: make the sons of Israel cautious (eulabēs). Fathers (patēr) of monasteries (monastērion), therefore, of those in the province (eparchia) of the Thebans, devout (eulabēs) men and having a not unwonderful (athaumastos) way of life (politeia), having come into Alexandria, and being asked by me the condition (katastasis) of the monasteries there, were telling (didaskō) that many are made to stumble (skandalizō) through such a cause (aitia). (a) Concerning not ordaining (cheirotoneō) without examination (anexetastōs). Some having newly married (gameō), and as it were having come down (katabainō) from the very bridal chambers (nymphōn), hastily carry along (synarpazō) some of the most God loving (theophilestatos) [sentence continues in the next section: bishops].
pass_b_english: By the same, to the bishops in Libya and the Pentapolis.

We must take care over everything that is useful and needful for building up the people, and that also contributes to the good name of the holy churches. For it is written, “Make the children of Israel careful” (Leviticus 15:31). Now fathers of monasteries in the province of the Thebaid, devout men whose way of life deserves admiration, came to Alexandria; and when I asked them about the state of the monasteries there, they told me that many are taking offence, for the following reason.
1. That no one should be ordained without examination
Some men who have only just married, and who have come down, as it were, straight from the bridal chamber, sweep along some of the most God-loving…

Ad episcopos qui sunt in Libya et Pentapoli
ΤΟΥ ΑΥΤΟΥ ΤΟΙΣ ΚΑΤΑ ΛΙΒΥΗΝ ΚΑΙ ΠΕΝΤΑΠΟΛΙΝ ΕΠΙΣΚΟΠΟΙΣ ∆
[Προοίμιον]
Παντὸς τοῦ χρησίμου καὶ ἀναγκαίου πρὸς οἰκοδομὴν τῶν λαῶν, τελοῦντος
δὲ καὶ εἰς ὑπόληψιν τῶν ἁγίων ἐκκλησιῶν, φροντίδα ποιεῖσθαι χρή· γέγραπται γάρ,
ὅτι εὐλαβεῖς ποιεῖτε τοὺς υἱοὺς Ἰσραήλ. Μοναστηρίων τοίνυν πατέρες τῶν κατὰ τὴν
Θηβαίων ἐπαρχίαν, ἄνδρες εὐλαβεῖς καὶ 282 οὐκ ἀθαύμαστον ἔχοντες πολιτείαν
, ἐλθόντες ἐν Ἀλεξανδρείᾳ, ἐρωτώμενοί τε παρ' ἐμοῦ τὴν κατάστασιν τῶν αὐτόσε
μοναστηρίων, ἐδίδασκον ὅτι σκανδαλίζονται πολλοὶ διὰ τοιαύτην αἰτίαν.
(α) Περὶ τοῦ ἀνεξετάστως μὴ χειροτονεῖν. Νεωστὶ γεγαμηκότες τινὲς καὶ
οἷον ἐξ αὐτῶν καταβάντες τῶν νυμφώνων, συναρπάζουσί τινας τῶν θεοφιλεστάτων
reviewer: claude (Wave A review, clause by clause against the Greek)
review_notes: Replaces a scaffold row ('Lemma-led open …' with copied Greek); the section had no real English before Wave A.
Checked clause by clause against the Greek: 'Παντὸς τοῦ χρησίμου καὶ ἀναγκαίου πρὸς οἰκοδομὴν τῶν λαῶν' = 'everything that is useful and needful for building up the people'.
Reviewer rv0 fix applied before merge: τελοῦντος ... εἰς ὑπόληψιν rendered 'contributes to the good name' rather than the weaker 'bears on'.
Scripture: Leviticus 15:31 checked against the LXX wording; citation placed inline beside the quotation.
Not rendered: the Latin file label, the collection sign ∆ and the page marker 282. The edition headings ([Προοίμιον], (α)) are rendered as headings.
